Buchi AutomataStay Tuned!





Explanation

Dr Strange represents the Buchi automata (NBA) and he is bargaining with Dormammu (infinite words over \(\Sigma\), i.e., \(\Sigma^\omega\)). The acceptance criterion of an NBA is that on “running” the infinite word through the automata in a non-deterministic fashion, accepting states must be visited infinitely many times during the entire run. This is similar to what Dr Strange does in the movie: he repeatedly revives himself using the time stone visiting the state “Dormammu, I have come to bargain” infinitely often.

Nowadays I feel as connected to olympiad geometry as the discrete topology.

Used during IMOTC 2026; some students had dropped syrup from the refreshments on their answer sheets which stuck consecutive pages together to form – you guessed it – a torus. They had to be warned that topological repair can be destructive so do not rely on it.

title: About Me
text:
How I looked a couple of years ago




Hi, I am Bhavya Tiwari, a third year student at IIT Bombay in the Computer Science and Engineering department. My interests broadly lie at the intersection of mathematics and theoretical CS. Over time I have become less of a math purist and like to explore areas at the intersection of multiple fields. Currently I am exploring multiples specks in the ocean of knowledge. I don’t really have any fixed hobbies but I do enjoy watching good science fiction movies and reading up on Indian Philosophy.










If I were a Springer-Verlag Graduate Text in Mathematics, I would be W.B.R. Lickorish’s An Introduction to Knot Theory.


I am an introduction to mathematical Knot Theory; the theory of knots and links of simple closed curves in three-dimensional space. I consist of a selection of topics which graduate students have found to be a successful introduction to the field. Three distinct techniques are employed; Geometric Topology Manoeuvres, Combinatorics, and Algebraic Topology.

title: Bhavya's Homepage
text: Today we went on a trip to Pondicherry and also had a bit of a debate about some religious issues. I believe the ideal of God is the mother of all ideas. Everybody follows some philosophy, and that might not be explicitly following a written philosophy. However, some things can be established with reasonable rigor, and a lack of knowledge of them causes many difficulties when trying to put things into practice. Today, for unknown reasons, I felt a profound sense of respect for this life for just existing here. Now, the ancient wisdom holds that this existence is bondage. We are in the material world, they say, having pain and blah blah. I do not know what or why I feel this, but perhaps it is some deep intuition that has given me a curious purpose. We abuse so many of these subtle things. Rather than looking at them as tools of bondage, we should look at them as the means of liberation of the soul. Hence, they should be respected, not disregarded, or something; they have their own purpose, which is best fulfilled when they are used in the right manner.
